## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
When --preserve-source-ids translates a dotted subtask id to a fresh flat id (QCLI-160), the preview's mappings field lists every record -- unchanged and renumbered alike -- with no field or section that isolates the ones where targetIdentifier != sourceIdentifier. A consumer has to diff the whole list by hand to find what actually changes. opum-agent did exactly that against its own live preview on 2026-09-02, misread the diff as a data hazard, and briefed four fleet sessions on a problem the tool's own alias-retention already handled -- direct evidence the current shape makes the wrong thing easy to see and the right thing (what changes vs. what doesn't) easy to miss, in a command whose entire job is telling someone what is about to happen to their data.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- AC:BEGIN -->
- [ ] #1 migration backlog preview's output (with --preserve-source-ids) includes a distinct, itemized list of mappings where targetIdentifier differs from sourceIdentifier, separate from the full mappings list
- [ ] #2 each entry in that list is intelligible without cross-referencing the aliases array -- it is visibly a renumbered/translated pair, not just two id strings
- [ ] #3 the existing mappings field is unchanged (additive, not breaking) so any current consumer parsing it keeps working
- [ ] #4 an e2e test previews a source mix of flat and dotted ids and asserts the new section lists exactly the translated ones, no more and no fewer
- [ ] #5 quest migration backlog preview --help's summary is updated to mention the new section
<!-- AC:END -->

plan: Add a BacklogRenumberedMapping interface (sourceIdentifier, targetIdentifier, reason) and an optional renumbered field on BacklogPreview, additive alongside the existing mappings field -- never included in the digest fingerprint since it is purely derived from data already hashed.

In previewWithPreservedIds, derive renumbered from mappings where targetIdentifier !== sourceIdentifier (only the dotted-subtask-translated case in preserve mode); leave it absent on the non-preserve (positional) path where every record renumbers and the section would be meaningless.
Update the migration backlog preview --help summary (command-help.ts) to mention the new renumbered section.

Add an e2e test previewing a source mix of flat and dotted ids under --preserve-source-ids, asserting renumbered lists exactly the translated pairs -- no more, no fewer -- and that mappings is unchanged/still carries every record.
implementationNotes: AC1/AC3: added a BacklogRenumberedMapping interface and an optional 'renumbered' field on BacklogPreview, populated only in previewWithPreservedIds (--preserve-source-ids mode) as the subset of mappings where targetIdentifier !== sourceIdentifier -- the only translation case in that mode is a dotted subtask minted a fresh flat id. mappings itself is untouched (still every record); renumbered is purely derived from it and deliberately excluded from the digest fingerprint, so apply --digest's CAS precondition is unaffected. AC2: each entry carries reason:'dotted_subtask_translated' alongside sourceIdentifier/targetIdentifier, so it reads as a translated pair on its own without cross-referencing aliases. AC4: extended the existing preserve-source-ids e2e test's flat+dotted mixed fixture (ODOC-1 flat, three dotted variants, one different-family exclusion) with assertions that renumbered lists exactly the three dotted-origin pairs -- no more, no fewer -- with the right reason and a changed id, while mappings stays at all 6 records. AC5: updated migration backlog preview --help's summary to mention the new field and that mappings is unchanged. Verified: bun run check 428/428 tests green (this branch predates QCLI-226's docs merge, hence 428 not 430 here).
finalSummary: migration backlog preview --preserve-source-ids now returns an additive 'renumbered' field: exactly the mappings whose id actually changed (dotted-subtask-to-flat translation), each labeled with a reason so it's legible on its own -- the report's core complaint, that a consumer had to diff the full mappings list by hand to find what changes, is fixed by isolating that set directly rather than requiring the diff. mappings itself is unchanged; renumbered is excluded from the digest since it's purely derived. Verified with an e2e test against a real mixed flat/dotted fixture, plus a --help summary update. bun run check: 428/428 tests green.
